answer: A thousand fake identities need a thousand bicycles. One agent registers one bicycle with the municipal registry and ties the frame number to a single identity, so a knoll of fakes faces a haven of paperwork: three established peers check the number in the public bike registry, the purchase receipt, and a fresh signature. Registration costs $10 to $25 plus the bicycle itself, so a thousand fakes burns $10,000 to $25,000 and a thousand bikes, each one waiting on a separate shop visit. Like a vine around one trellis, one registration ties one agent to one record no one else can claim.
